evals.prompt: I'm reviewing a PR that adds four new tools: fetch_skill, search_skills, describe_skill, read_skill_file. My instinct is that this should just be one skill_lookup tool with an action parameter, since I've read that agents get confused by too many similar tools. Should I push back on this PR?
evals.expected_output: Applies the consolidation guidance correctly by checking what axis the tools actually split on (what the caller already knows / how much it should pay) rather than reflexively applying 'fewer tools is better'. Concludes the four-tool split is likely defensible if it's not near-duplicate verbs on the same resource, and explains why via the ResponseFormat/cost-tiering analogy, rather than agreeing with the reviewer's instinct by default.
expectations: Identifies the actual axis the four tools split on (what the caller knows / cost tiering) rather than just counting tools
References the ResponseFormat concise/detailed pattern or an equivalent cost-tiering analogy
Does not recommend merging the four tools into one without qualification
Gives the PR reviewer an actual recommendation (push back or don't) with reasoning
